preview: Sarvesh Shirude shares his interview experience for an internship at HDFC Bank, detailing the selection process consisting of an online application, CV short-listing, and a personal interview covering OOPS, DBMS, and HR questions.
content: Interview Experience Sarvesh Shirude , B.Tech Electronics 2020-24 HDFC Bank visited our campus for the first time to offer internships for 3rd year students. Candidates from all branches were eligible to apply for this internship. There were 3 rounds of the selection process: 1. Online Application: For this, we need to complete our profile on the Superset platform, and from there apply for the internship. 2. CV Short-listing: Shortlisting for interviews was supposed to be done through this round. The final date scheduled for interviews is September 6th, so we expected to receive shortlisting by September 5th, but it didn’t go according that way due to some issues. But literally, the shortlisting came on September 6th, around 1 PM, and everyone seemed to be in a panic. A total of 45 candidates were shortlisted, surprisingly from either the CS or Electronics branch, and we were told to have only one interview round. (The important part here is to hold our nerves as the shortlisting came on the day of the interview itself, so it’s really important to keep ourselves calm and try to be in the situation.) 3. Personal Interview: As expected, the interview started with the “Introduce yourself” question. (Be prepared with your introduction beforehand, as this is the most common interview question.) Then he asked me about my family background details and my short-term and long-term goals. Next, he moved on to the Technical part and asked me in which programming language you are comfortable, I answered “C++” and the discussion went ahead with basic OOPS questions which are, ●Why and where do we use OOPS?? ●What are the 4 pillars of OOPS? and further asked me to explain Polymorphism. Then he asked me what is the difference between Primary Key &. Foreign Key?? But I was not able to answer this very basic question😔. He then asked me to explain my project. I had prepared for this question, so I explained to him the entire process of how I built this project. (But I was not sure whether he was satisfied with my project or not.) Then he asked me which job role you are interested in. I said Software Developer, and then his follow-up question was, "We are not offering you that job role. Then why do you still want to join our organization? " (I thought that this was going to be the deciding question, so I took a few seconds and then answered this question.) I said, Sir, as a fresher I would like to explore this field as well and I am sure by working at your esteemed organization I am going to upskill myself, so it would be a great opportunity for me to work with HDFC Bank. (I think he was satisfied with my answer.) Lastly, he asked me, "Do you have any questions for me?" I asked him, ●How was your experience of working with HDFC Bank so far?? ●Which Tech Stack is used for the projects on which Interns work?? (In every interview experience I read about our seniors, they always mentioned asking questions because it feels like we are interested in that company, so do ask questions.) Finally, the results were announced on 15th September. A total of 11 candidates were selected, and I was fortunate enough to be one of them😊 Important Tips: ❖I thought HDFC would carry out an Online Assessment test but they didn’t. But for aptitude preparation, I solely followed Indiabix. Many companies ask questions from Arithmetic aptitude, Logical reasoning, verbal ability sections, so you can practice questions from there. ❖For OOPS, you can follow Coding Ninjas: OOPS in C++, Interviewbit, and for core CS subjects like DBMS and OS, you can refer to Gate Smashers. ❖For learning DSA, I followed the Love Babbar course, and for problem-solving, I used 450 dsa, Striver’s SDE Sheet. ❖It’s not about knowing everything every time during the interview, we must be confident enough to answer the questions and try to be in the situation. ❖Prepare for famous interview questions like Introduce yourself, always have some idea about the company you are appearing for the interview and remember to ask questions to the interviewer at the end. ❖Luck is a very important factor, so don’t get discouraged if you get rejected by a company. Results will fall accordingly if you believe in your preparation. “Gaining knowledge is the first step to wisdom, sharing it is the first step to humanity”.
